```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# The fit takes about 35 minutes on 8 cores (97,806 occasions) and the
# cross-validation 50 fits on AWS, so the results were saved by
# dev/precompute-dynamic.R and dev/dyn-kfold/ and are read from
# dynamic-results.rds.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%")
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "C"))   # month names in English
library(crywolf)
res <- readRDS("dynamic-results.rds")
row <- function(var) res$summary[res$summary$variable == var, ]
ci <- function(var, digits = 2) {
  r <- row(var)
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"),
          r$mean, r$lower, r$upper)
}
cv <- res$cv$total
pika <- res$pika
pal <- c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#E69F00")
fig_theme <- ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
pika_ci <- function(var, digits = 2) {
  r <- pika$summary[pika$summary$variable == var, ]
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"), r$mean, r$lower, r$upper)
}
prob_ci <- function(var) {
  r <- pika$summary[pika$summary$variable == var, ]
  sprintf("%.3f (%.3f to %.3f)", plogis(r$mean), plogis(r$lower), plogis(r$upper))
}
long_draws <- function(d) {
  data.frame(variable = rep(names(d), each = nrow(d)), value = unlist(d, use.names = FALSE))
}
pair <- function(name) {
  r <- res$cv$pairs[res$cv$pairs$comparison == name, ]
  sprintf("%.1f (SE %.1f)", r$diff, r$se)
}
```

```{r stale, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(crywolf:::.stale_note(res, "dynamic-results.rds"))
```

The other articles on the `curiango` data (Piatti et al., 2026) treat each
site-night as an independent site. A recorder that picked up the Common
Pauraque last night is then no more likely to pick it up tonight than one
that has been silent for a month. `fp_occu_dyn()` drops that assumption. It
fits the dynamic occupancy model (MacKenzie et al., 2003) with the false
positives of the multiple-methods design (Miller et al., 2013), with the
nights of each site as seasons. This article fits it to the `curiango`
data, compares it with the model of independent site-nights by blocked
cross-validation, reports how it behaved in simulations, and applies it to a
second data set.

## The model

Each site $i$ is in use ($z_{it} = 1$) or not ($z_{it} = 0$) on night $t$.
On the first night, $\Pr(z_{i1} = 1) = \psi_1$. On every later night, the
state follows a Markov chain:

$$
\Pr(z_{it} = 1 \mid z_{i,t-1} = 0) = \gamma_{it}, \qquad
\Pr(z_{it} = 0 \mid z_{i,t-1} = 1) = \epsilon_{it},
$$

where the colonization $\gamma_{it}$ and the extinction $\epsilon_{it}$
have logit-linear predictors (`col` and `ext`). Within a night, the
observation model is that of `fp_occu()`: true detections with probability
$p_{11}$ on nights in use, false positives with probability $p_{10}$ on
every night, and verified recordings that settle what was recorded. The
states are summed out by the forward algorithm, so the model has no latent
discrete parameters for Stan to sample.

```{r dag, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Directed acyclic graph of the model fitted by `fp_occu_dyn()`. Hexagons are priors (defaults of `fp_priors()`), yellow ellipses are parameters, blue boxes are covariates, green ellipses are latent quantities and linear predictors, and octagons are the observed data. Dashed outlines mark optional components. The false-positive coefficients are called eta here because gamma is colonization. The options `markov`, `random_det` and `random_fp` are not drawn."}
knitr::include_graphics("dynamic-dag.png")
```

With nights as seasons, "occupancy" means use of the site on a given
night. Colonization is the start of use after a night without it, and
extinction is the end of use after a night with it. Neither is a change in
the population of the site.

`fp_data(season = )` takes the column of the night. When the seasons are
dates, it fills in the dates without data, so that every transition spans
one night. A site without data on a night contributes to that night only
through the transitions. In `curiango`, the nights run from 25 November
2023 to 26 February 2025, with between
`r min(res$sites_per_night)` and `r max(res$sites_per_night)` of the seven
sites recorded on each night.

## Fitting

The colonization and the extinction depend on the temperature and relative
humidity of the night. Transitions into nights without data need these
covariates too, so we use the mean over the sites recorded on each date
(`temp_d`, `rh_d`), passed as season covariates. Every date has at least
one site recorded. Detection depends on the soundscape indices of each
minute, and the false-positive rate on the temperature and humidity at the
site that night.

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
zs <- function(v) as.numeric(scale(v))
m <- curiango$minutes
nt <- curiango$nights
daily <- aggregate(cbind(temp, rh) ~ night, nt, mean)
daily <- data.frame(night = daily$night, temp_d = zs(daily$temp), rh_d = zs(daily$rh))
i <- match(m$site_night, nt$site_night)
auto <- data.frame(site = m$site, night = nt$night[i], time = m$time,
                   y = as.integer(m$conf_custom >= 0.40),
                   bio = zs(m$bio), aci = zs(m$aci),
                   temp = zs(nt$temp[i]), rh = zs(nt$rh[i]), recorder = m$site)
ver <- data.frame(site = curiango$verified$site,
                  night = nt$night[match(curiango$verified$site_night, nt$site_night)],
                  y = curiango$verified$y)
d <- fp_data(auto, data.frame(site = unique(auto$site)), ver, site = "site",
             recorder = "recorder", season = "night", season_covs = daily)

fit <- fp_occu_dyn(d, psi1 = ~ 1, col = ~ temp_d + rh_d, ext = ~ temp_d + rh_d,
                   det = ~ bio + aci, fp = ~ temp + rh, threads_per_chain = 2)
```

The fit took about `r round(res$minutes)` minutes with four chains of two
threads. It converged: the largest R-hat was
`r sprintf("%.3f", res$diagnostics$max_rhat)`, the smallest bulk effective
sample size `r round(res$diagnostics$min_ess_bulk)`, with
`r res$diagnostics$divergences` divergent transitions.

## Results

```{r estimates, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Posterior distributions of the parameters of `curiango`, from 1,000 draws. Points are medians, and the thick and thin bars are the 66% and 95% intervals. Coefficients are on the logit scale, and the dashed line marks zero."}
est <- long_draws(res$draws)
est$panel <- factor(ifelse(startsWith(est$variable, "col_"), "Colonization (logit)",
                    ifelse(startsWith(est$variable, "ext_"), "Extinction (logit)", est$variable)),
                    c("Colonization (logit)", "Extinction (logit)", "p11_ref", "p10_ref"))
est$term <- factor(ifelse(grepl("Intercept", est$variable), "Intercept",
                   ifelse(grepl("temp", est$variable), "Temperature",
                   ifelse(grepl("rh", est$variable), "Humidity", " "))),
                   c(" ", "Humidity", "Temperature", "Intercept"))
zero <- data.frame(panel = factor(c("Colonization (logit)", "Extinction (logit)"), levels(est$panel)),
                   x = 0)
ggplot2::ggplot(est, ggplot2::aes(value, term)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(ggplot2::aes(xintercept = x), zero, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(fill = pal[1], alpha = 0.8, .width = c(0.66, 0.95), point_size = 1.5,
                       normalize = "groups") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  fig_theme
```

On a night of average temperature and humidity, a site not in use starts
being used with probability
`r sprintf("%.3f", plogis(row("col_(Intercept)")$mean))`. A site in use
stops with probability
`r sprintf("%.2f", plogis(row("ext_(Intercept)")$mean))`, so a spell of use
lasts about `r round(1 / plogis(row("ext_(Intercept)")$mean), 1)` nights
on average. Humid nights start fewer spells: the humidity coefficient of
colonization is `r ci("col_rh_d")`. Its coefficient of extinction,
`r ci("ext_rh_d")`, points to humid nights also ending spells, but its
interval reaches zero. The intervals of both temperature coefficients
include zero.

A minute of a night in use
yields a true detection with probability `r ci("p11_ref", 3)` at the
reference values. A minute yields a false positive with probability
`r ci("p10_ref", 4)`.

The model also estimates, for each night, the fraction of the seven sites
in use (`psi_fs`, from the states sampled given all the data). On nights
when a site was not recorded, its state is inferred from the nights around
it.

```{r psi-fs, fig.cap = "Fraction of the seven sites in use on each night (posterior mean and 95% interval of psi_fs)."}
fs <- res$summary[grepl("^psi_fs\\[", res$summary$variable), ]
fs$night <- as.Date(fs$season)
ggplot2::ggplot(fs, ggplot2::aes(night, mean)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "#2DE2E6",
                       alpha = 0.4) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Fraction of sites in use") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

`fp_sites()` gives, for each site and night, the probability that the site
was in use given all its data:

```{r use, fig.height = 3, fig.cap = "Probability that each site was in use on each night given all the data. Nights without recordings at a site are paler."}
s <- res$sites
rec <- paste(s$site, s$night) %in% paste(curiango$nights$site, curiango$nights$night)
s$recorded <- ifelse(rec, "recorded", "not recorded")
ggplot2::ggplot(s, ggplot2::aes(as.Date(night), site, fill = occupied, alpha = recorded)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  ggplot2::scale_alpha_manual(values = c(recorded = 1, "not recorded" = 0.35)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Pr(in use)", alpha = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

### Posterior predictive check

The posterior predictive check compares the detections of each site-night
with those replicated from the fit. It gives p = `r res$ppc$p_value`: the
observed discrepancy (median `r round(stats::median(res$ppc$fit_obs))`)
exceeds the replicated one (median
`r round(stats::median(res$ppc$fit_rep))`) on every draw. The model of
independent site-nights fails this check by a similar margin
(`vignette("markov")`). The misfit therefore lies within nights, where the
minutes are taken as independent, and not in the dynamics across nights.
`fp_occu_dyn(markov = )` adds the Markov term of `vignette("markov")` for
runs of detections within a night. The next section compares it by
cross-validation.

## Comparison with independent site-nights

LOO cannot compare the two models here. The log-likelihood of
`fp_occu_dyn()` has one value per site, because the nights of a site are
not independent. With seven sites, leaving one out would remove a seventh
of the data at a time.

Instead, we cross-validated on blocks of nights. The dates were cut into
weeks, and the weeks were dealt at random into ten folds, the same for
every site. The first and the last week stayed in every training set, so
that every fit spans the same nights. Each model was fitted ten times, each
time without one fold. For the dynamic model, the left-out nights became
nights without data, whose states are predicted from the neighbouring
nights. The model of independent site-nights used the same detection,
false-positive and recorder terms, with `occ ~ temp_d + rh_d`. The score of
each site and fold is the log of the posterior predictive density of its
left-out minutes and verified recordings (elpd).

The comparison has five models. `dyn` is the fit above and `ind` the model of
independent site-nights. `dyn_mk` and `ind_mk` add `markov = "time"`.
`ind_rd` adds `random_det` to `ind`, a detection effect for each site-night,
which competes with the dynamics for the variation between nights.

```{r cv, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2.6, fig.cap = "Difference in elpd from `dyn` in the blocked cross-validation. Bars are two standard errors of the difference, and `dyn` itself has none."}
cvd <- cv[order(cv$diff_from_dyn), ]
cvd$model <- factor(cvd$model, cvd$model)
ggplot2::ggplot(cvd, ggplot2::aes(diff_from_dyn, model)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(xmin = diff_from_dyn - 2 * se_diff,
                                        xmax = diff_from_dyn + 2 * se_diff),
                           colour = pal[1], size = 0.4) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "elpd difference from dyn", y = NULL) +
  fig_theme
```

The dynamic model predicts the left-out nights better than the independent
one, by `r pair("dyn - ind")` in elpd over `r res$cv_units` site and fold units.
The same holds with the Markov term, by `r pair("dyn_mk - ind_mk")`.
The Markov term itself gains more than the dynamics:
`r pair("ind_mk - ind")` over `ind`. The two gains add up, and `dyn_mk` has the
highest elpd in all ten folds and at all seven sites:

```{r cv-site, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Gain in elpd over `ind` at each site and in each fold. Positive values favour the model over independent site-nights."}
gain <- function(x, id, label) {
  m <- c("dyn", "dyn_mk", "ind_mk", "ind_rd")
  do.call(rbind, lapply(m, function(k) {
    data.frame(unit = as.character(x[[id]]), model = k, panel = label,
               gain = x[[paste0("elpd.", k)]] - x$elpd.ind)
  }))
}
g <- rbind(gain(res$cv$by_site, "site", "By site"), gain(res$cv$by_fold, "fold", "By fold"))
g$unit <- factor(g$unit, c(sort(unique(res$cv$by_site$site)), 10:1))
g$panel <- factor(g$panel, c("By site", "By fold"))
ggplot2::ggplot(g, ggplot2::aes(gain, unit, colour = model, shape = model)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = pal[1:4]) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "elpd gain over ind", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  fig_theme + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

`random_det` also improves on `ind`, by `r pair("ind_rd - ind")`, but less than
the Markov term does. Runs of detections, then, explain more of these data than
differences between nights alone.

Three caveats apply. The SE treats the site and fold units as independent,
although the units of a fold share a training fit, so it is likely too
small. Each left-out week has nights in the training data on both
sides, so the dynamic model interpolates as well as forecasts. And the elpd of
`ind_rd` comes from 400 posterior draws, because integrating its effects is
slow, against 4,000 for the other models. All 50 training fits converged; one
fit of the independent model was rerun with another seed after a chain stuck
in a second mode (see `dev/dyn-kfold/README.md` in the source repository).

## Validation in simulation

We simulated data with `simulate_fp_dyn()` and fitted the model to them, in
6,320 tasks, with none ending in error. The criteria were set before the
results, and the tables are in `dev/dyn-val/` in the source repository.
All the designs had 100 sites.

With p11 of at least 0.30 and at least 10% of site-seasons verified, the model
was well calibrated. Coverage of the 95% intervals of initial occupancy,
colonization, extinction, `p10_bar` and `psi_fs` was at least 0.90, and the
absolute bias was at most 0.024. Observation-confirmation, with 10% or 30% of
occasions confirmed, met the same thresholds. Simulation-based calibration
found no departure from uniform ranks in 1,000 replicates.

```{r val-bias, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Bias of the posterior mean in the designs with low detection, by the fraction of site-seasons verified. Dashed lines mark the threshold of 0.05."}
lowp <- res$val$lowp
lowp$p11 <- factor(lowp$p11)
lowp$seasons <- factor(paste(lowp$nseason, "seasons"), paste(c(3, 6, 10), "seasons"))
val_plot <- function(y, line, label) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(lowp, ggplot2::aes(frac_verified, .data[[y]], colour = p11, shape = p11)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = line, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = pal[1:2]) +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(param ~ seasons) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Fraction of site-seasons verified", y = label) +
    fig_theme + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
val_plot("bias", c(-0.05, 0.05), "Bias")
```

```{r val-coverage, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Coverage of the 95% intervals in the same designs. The dashed line marks the threshold of 0.90."}
val_plot("coverage", 0.90, "Coverage")
```

The limits lie at low detection with little verification:

* With p11 = 0.15 and no verification, colonization was biased upwards by 0.12
  to 0.17 and extinction by 0.09 to 0.13, and up to 40% of fits did not converge.
* With p11 = 0.15 and 10% verified, both biases stayed above 0.05 with 3 or 6
  seasons, and fell below it with 10 seasons.
* With p11 = 0.15 and 20% or more verified, the thresholds were met.

```{r val-converged, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2.8, fig.cap = "Fraction of the fits of each design cell with R-hat below 1.01. Each point is a cell, and the dashed line marks the threshold of 0.95."}
cells <- res$val$lowp_fits
cells$p11 <- factor(cells$p11)
ggplot2::ggplot(cells, ggplot2::aes(factor(frac_verified), converged, colour = p11, shape = p11)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0.95, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(position = ggplot2::position_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0, seed = 1), alpha = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = pal[1:2]) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Fraction of site-seasons verified", y = "Fits converged") +
  fig_theme
```

Ignoring a source of variation was costly. When false positives varied with a
covariate, `fp ~ 1` kept `psi_fs` nearly unbiased (at most 0.018), but the
coverage of `p10_bar` fell to between 0.72 and 0.89. When site effects on
detection had an SD of 1, leaving out `random_det` gave a bias of -0.10 in
`psi_fs` and a coverage of 0.01. With runs of detections of strength 2 on the
logit scale, leaving out `markov` gave a coverage of 0.44 for `psi_fs`.
With the option on, both models recovered these quantities, with a coverage of
at least 0.90 for `sd_det_site` and `det_y_prev`.

```{r val-omit, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Coverage of the 95% intervals when the data have a source of variation and the model leaves it out or includes it. The dashed line marks the threshold of 0.90. False positives on a covariate are shown for the design with 20% of site-seasons verified."}
one <- function(x, scenario, on) {
  data.frame(scenario = scenario, param = x$param, coverage = x$coverage,
             model = ifelse(x$model == on, "Included", "Left out"))
}
ca <- res$val$calib
ca <- ca[ca$b_fp == 1 & ca$frac_verified == 0.2, ]
ra <- res$val$randet
ma <- res$val$markov
om <- rbind(one(ca, "fp on a covariate", "fp_x"),
            one(ra[ra$sd_det == 0.5, ], "Site effects, SD 0.5", "random_det"),
            one(ra[ra$sd_det == 1, ], "Site effects, SD 1", "random_det"),
            one(ma[ma$a == 1, ], "Runs, strength 1", "markov"),
            one(ma[ma$a == 2, ], "Runs, strength 2", "markov"))
om <- om[om$param %in% c("col", "ext", "p10_bar", "psi_fs", "psi1"), ]
om$scenario <- factor(om$scenario, unique(om$scenario))
ggplot2::ggplot(om, ggplot2::aes(coverage, param, colour = model, shape = model)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0.90, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = pal[1:2]) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ scenario, ncol = 2) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Coverage", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  fig_theme + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

With strong site effects, `random_det` needed longer chains. With an SD of 1 and
1,000 + 1,000 iterations, 93% of fits reached R-hat below 1.01. With 2,000 +
2,000 iterations on the same data, 99% did, and the estimates did not change.

## A second data set

We also fitted the model to surveys of the American pika (*Ochotona princeps*)
by Goldman et al. (2023), with 771 plots in five park units from 2010 to 2021.
Years are the seasons, and 2015 and 2016 are seasons without data. Each survey
gives one occasion for each ambiguous sign (fresh scat, fresh haypile, call), with
the sign as a covariate of `det` and `fp`. Sightings and unambiguous fresh scat
form the verified method. Unlike the article, this model does not give each sign
its own detection process.

The dynamic model has `psi1 ~ park`, with constant colonization and extinction.
The independent model treats each plot-year as a site, with `occ ~ park + year`.
All five fits had no divergent transitions, R-hat of at most
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(sapply(pika$diagnostics, "[[", "max_rhat")))`, and a bulk
effective sample size of at least
`r round(min(sapply(pika$diagnostics, "[[", "min_ess_bulk")))`.

```{r pika-rates, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 3.6, fig.cap = "Posterior distributions of the rates of the pika model, from 1,000 draws. `psi_eq` is the occupancy implied by colonization and extinction at equilibrium."}
pr <- pika$draws
pr[c("col_(Intercept)", "ext_(Intercept)")] <- lapply(pr[c("col_(Intercept)", "ext_(Intercept)")], plogis)
names(pr)[1:2] <- c("Colonization", "Extinction")
pr <- long_draws(pr)
pr$variable <- factor(pr$variable, unique(pr$variable))
ggplot2::ggplot(pr, ggplot2::aes(value)) +
  ggdist::stat_halfeye(fill = pal[1], alpha = 0.8, .width = c(0.66, 0.95), point_size = 1.5,
                       normalize = "panels") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Probability", y = NULL) +
  fig_theme
```

Colonization was `r prob_ci("col_(Intercept)")` and extinction
`r prob_ci("ext_(Intercept)")` per year. Occupancy at equilibrium was
`r pika_ci("psi_eq")`. A call, the reference sign, was recorded on a survey of an
occupied plot with probability `r pika_ci("p11_ref")`, and on a survey of an
unoccupied plot with probability `r pika_ci("p10_ref", 3)`. Goldman et al.
(2023) report about 0.06 for both colonization and extinction with a different
model, so the comparison is only of order of magnitude.

```{r pika-occ, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 3.4, fig.cap = "Mean probability that the plots of each park unit were occupied in each year, given all the data. The shaded years have no surveys, so their states come from the years around them."}
occ <- pika$occ_park
occ$year <- as.numeric(as.character(occ$year))
ggplot2::ggplot(occ, ggplot2::aes(year, occupied, colour = park, shape = park)) +
  ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = 2014.5, xmax = 2016.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey92") +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2021, 2)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Pr(occupied)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  fig_theme
```

Occupancy moved towards the equilibrium in most park units. Colonization and
extinction are constant and shared in this model, so that movement is built in. It
is not evidence of a trend in any park unit.

The posterior predictive checks gave p = `r sprintf("%.2f", pika$ppc$dyn_auto$p_value)`
for the automated method and p = `r sprintf("%.2f", pika$ppc$dyn_ver$p_value)` for the
verified one, so the misfit seen on `curiango` did not appear here. The independent
model gave p = `r sprintf("%.2f", pika$ppc$ind_auto$p_value)` for the automated method.

```{r pika-ppc, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 2.8, fig.cap = "Posterior predictive checks of the pika models. Each point is a draw, and points on the line have equal observed and replicated discrepancies."}
pp <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(x, label) {
  data.frame(check = sprintf("%s (p = %.2f)", label, x$p_value), obs = x$fit_obs, rep = x$fit_rep)
}, pika$ppc, c("dyn, automated", "dyn, verified", "ind, automated")))
pp$check <- factor(pp$check, unique(pp$check))
ggplot2::ggplot(pp, ggplot2::aes(obs, rep)) +
  ggplot2::geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(colour = pal[1], alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ check, scales = "free") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Observed discrepancy", y = "Replicated discrepancy") +
  fig_theme
```

Prior means of 1 to 3 for `fp_gap`, and a doubled prior SD, left the estimates
nearly unchanged.

```{r pika-priors, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 3.6, fig.cap = "Posterior means and 95% intervals of the pika model under four priors of `fp_gap`, on the scale of each parameter."}
se <- pika$sensitivity
se <- se[se$variable %in% c("col_(Intercept)", "ext_(Intercept)", "fp_gap", "p11_ref", "p10_ref", "psi_eq"), ]
se$prior <- factor(se$prior, c("gap_wide", "gap_high", "gap_low", "default"),
                   c("mean 2, SD 3", "mean 3", "mean 1", "default"))
ggplot2::ggplot(se, ggplot2::aes(mean, prior)) +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper), colour = pal[1], size = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  fig_theme
```

Leaving out whole plots, PSIS-LOO favoured the dynamic model over independent
plot-years by `r sprintf("%.1f (SE %.1f)", -pika$loo$elpd_diff[2], pika$loo$se_diff[2])` in
elpd, with no Pareto k above 0.7. With 771 plots, leaving one out removes little of
the data, which is why LOO works here and not on the seven sites of `curiango`.

Two simplifications matter. The verified occasion shares its survey with the
automated ones, and unambiguous scat is a subset of fresh scat, so the two methods
are not fully independent given the state. The sign also enters `det` and `fp` as a
covariate, whereas the article gives each sign its own model.

The data are in `pika`, and the script is in `dev/dyn-pika/` in the source repository.

## When to use it

* With repeated nights or visits at the same sites, use on one night is
  informative about the next, and the dynamic model uses that information.
* Each season needs covariates for the transitions into it, including
  seasons without data. Choose covariates that exist on every night.
* Compare with the independent model on blocks of seasons, not by LOO,
  whenever the sites are few.
* Verify recordings in at least 10% of site-seasons, and more when detection
  is low. Without verification, colonization and extinction are biased at low
  detection.
* Runs of detections are common in passive acoustic monitoring, where occasions
  are minutes close in time. Check for them and consider `markov`.
* `fp_calibrate()` simulates only single-season designs, so it does not plan a
  dynamic study; `simulate_fp_dyn()` is the starting point for that.
